deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X_0 is a scheme over a perfect field k of characteristic p>0, W = W(k), S = Spec W. Grothendieck considers the crystalline cohomology H^*((X_0/S)_cris, O) taken directly over S, rather than over the truncations S_n = Spec W_n. Over S, p is not nilpotent on the base, and p has divided powers in W. This is a graded W-module.

His initial hope was that this is 'the' right p-adic cohomology. The supporting argument runs as follows. Suppose X_0 is smooth and lifts to X smooth over W, under a simplifying hypothesis inserted in the margin; a word 'propre' seems to be struck out. Then, by the previous exposé (presumably the comparison theorem between crystalline and de Rham cohomology at finite level), one gets H^*((X_0/S)_cris, O) = lim_n H^*((X_n/S_n)_cris, O). He hoped that in the limit, perhaps modulo torsion, this would give lim_n H_DR(X_n/S_n) = H_DR(X/S), which is the 'excellent' object.

He then records that this is false. For an 'ordinary' smooth X_0/k, the naive H^i((X_0/S)_cris, O) vanishes for i > dim X_0, whereas the projective limit of the de Rham cohomologies is fine and lives in degrees up to 2 dim.

The next page diagnoses the cause. Working affine-locally, the projective limit does not commute with localisation by p (W -> K = W[1/p]). This is the familiar discrepancy between Zariski-local (non-complete) rings, p-adic completions, and inverting p. As a remedy he proposes a larger site of pro-infinitesimal thickenings by Washnitzer–Monsky (weakly complete) W-algebras B -> A_0, with nilpotent kernel modulo p. That is an early sketch of what became the Monsky–Washnitzer / overconvergent / rigid approach.

The point of the page is to explain why the naive 'crystalline site over W' is not the p-adic cohomology. The vanishing above dim X_0 suggests that the naive object only sees something like the slope-0 (unit-root, Witt-vector / étale p-adic) part, which for ordinary varieties is H^i(X_0, WO)_K ≅ H^i_et(X_0, Q_p) ⊗ K and vanishes for i > dim. The correct definition must be the limit over the S_n, i.e. Rlim, as in Berthelot's later theory.
errors: The equality H^*((X_0/S)_cris,O) = lim_n H^*((X_n/S_n)_cris,O) is asserted only under lifting and a 'simplifying hypothesis'. In general a lim^1 / Rlim term intervenes, and Grothendieck himself shows that the expected identification with H_DR(X/W) fails. The page is internally a record of a refuted hope, not an error.

The precise mechanism behind 'H^i = 0 for i > dim X_0 when X_0 is ordinary' is not justified on the page. It is consistent with the naive site only capturing the slope-0 (Witt-vector / unit-root) part, but the argument is not written out here and the exact site used (PD condition, whether p is locally nilpotent on objects) is ambiguous.

ideas.what: Crystalline cohomology taken directly over Spec W (p not nilpotent) versus the limit over W_n
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline cohomology H_cris(X_0/W) := Rlim H_cris(X_0/W_n); failure of the 'non-truncated' crystalline site
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); unsure of the exact statement there

ideas.what: Comparison of crystalline cohomology with de Rham cohomology of a smooth lift: lim H_DR(X_n/W_n) = H_DR(X/W)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; proved in detail by Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: For ordinary X_0 the naive cohomology vanishes above dim X_0, i.e. it only sees a 'Witt vector / unit-root' part
ideas.modern_name: Slope-0 part H^i(X, WO)_K ≅ H^i_et(X,Q_p)⊗K; Bloch–Illusie slope spectral sequence

ideas.what: Diagnosis: projective limit does not commute with inverting p, motivating weakly complete (Washnitzer–Monsky) algebras (next page)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Monsky–Washnitzer (1968), Berthelot (rigid cohomology, 1980s), Le Stum (overconvergent site, 2000s)

missed.claim: A documented, dated (1966-67) record of Grothendieck's initial hope that crystalline cohomology over W itself would be the p-adic cohomology, and his explicit counterexample: for ordinary X_0 it vanishes in degrees > dim X_0. This explains historically why the theory is defined as a limit over W_n. Combined with the next page, it shows him moving directly toward a Monsky–Washnitzer–style overconvergent site.
missed.quote: Mon espoir initial était qu'il soit "le" bon candidat pour une cohomologie p-adique ... C'est faux malheureusement. Par exemple si X_0/k est un schéma lisse "ordinaire" ... on trouve que H^i((X_0/S)_cris, O) = 0 si i > dim X_0 !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest. The observation that a naive integral site captures only a unit-root / slope-0 part anticipates later slope theory. The proposal on the next page is an early form of the overconvergent site (Le Stum) and of rigid cohomology.

deep.surprise_reason: The page records a refuted conjecture and an explicit counterexample showing why crystalline cohomology must be built from the W_n. This is a nice historical detail, and the link to unit-root / slope-0 phenomena for ordinary varieties is suggestive, but the mathematics is now standard. The more interesting overconvergent-site proposal lies on the following page.
